portInfo.description: Bonaire’s most rewarding distinction is between its living town, cultural villages and protected landscapes. Kralendijk’s Fort Oranje and former fish market make a compact first visit; Mangazina di Rei interprets rural heritage around Rincon. The southern slave huts and navigation obelisks should be read as evidence of salt production and forced labour, not treated only as a coastal photograph. Water access is not simply “free beach equals free snorkelling”. STINAPA requires a Nature Fee for marine/national-park users; its current park page quotes a one-day cruise-passenger fee ofUS$10, read 5 November 2026, but coverage/exemptions need direct confirmation. That is a conservation charge, not proof of a government visitor-entry-tax amount. The tourism guide’s broad annual-fee summary is not substituted for the operator’s cruise-specific rule.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
topThings: Fort Oranje, Fort Oranje, Kralendijk waterfront, Bonaire: A town-history landmark close to both cruise piers. Allow about 45 minutes (editorial estimate). Exterior/visitor access and any current working-building restrictions need checking.

Plasa Machi Mimi, Plasa Machi Mimi, former fish market, downtown Kralendijk: A named market-history meeting point for a local walk. Allow about 40 minutes (editorial estimate). Do not promise an active fish market or a daily craft-event schedule.

Mangazina di Rei, Mangazina di Rei cultural park, Rincon, Bonaire: Rural heritage, traditional crafts and community context. Allow about 90 minutes (editorial estimate). Confirm current programme/visitor entry; no permanent food service assumed.

Slave Huts and Obelisks, Slave Huts historic roadside visitor area, southern Bonaire: Interpretation of enslaved salt workers and maritime navigation. Allow about 60 minutes (editorial estimate). Actual selected hut/parking point must be agreed with the guide; Kaya Grandi#2 in the source footer is the tourism office, not this attraction.

1000 Steps, 1000 Steps named coastal access, northwestern Bonaire: A focused shore-view/optional licensed snorkel stop on the northern route. Allow about 90 minutes (editorial estimate). Steps, sea conditions and Nature Fee apply; the name is not a verified step count or an accessible ramp.
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Nature Fee, government entry tax and ship excursion price are not interchangeable. Confirm the cruise-specific conservation rule before any water or park use.
